title: The 2nd lord is in a kendra or trikona

text.en: The lord of the 2nd house sits in a kendra or trikona, which classical texts read as support for wealth and family resources.
text.impact: Money tends to stay with you. Income finds its way into savings, family resources and things you keep, rather than passing straight through.

source.note: Authored from general knowledge of a commonly taught Parashari principle and reviewed by AI at the product owner's direction. No textual citation has been verified; an astrologer may re-review.

review.reviewer: Claude (AI review at the product owner's direction)
review.comment: Core principle: a bhava lord in a kendra or trikona strengthens its bhava. Plain-language impact line added and reviewed 2026-09-22: it restates the same principle in everyday words, with what helps where the indication is difficult, and predicts no event.

title: The 2nd lord is in the 6th, 8th or 12th house

text.en: The lord of the 2nd house sits in a dusthana (the 6th, 8th or 12th), which classical texts read as strain on wealth and family resources.
text.impact: Money tends to go out about as fast as it comes in, with expenses, dues or family needs taking their share. Budgeting and keeping savings out of easy reach help more than simply earning more.

title: The 2nd lord is exalted, in moolatrikona or in its own sign

text.en: The lord of the 2nd house is exalted, in moolatrikona or in its own sign, and able to give its results fully.
text.impact: Resources hold. What you build up tends to last, and family means support you rather than drain you.

text.en: The lord of the 2nd house is debilitated, which classical texts read as difficulty with wealth and family resources, unless the debilitation is cancelled.
text.impact: Savings can be harder to hold on to than to earn, particularly in the early years. This points to habits worth building rather than to a fixed level of means.

title: The 11th lord is in the 6th, 8th or 12th house

text.en: The lord of the 11th house, the house of gains, sits in a dusthana, which classical texts read as gains that come with effort or are spent.
text.impact: Gains tend to come with effort, or later than expected. Income from steady work usually serves you better than anything promising quick returns.

title: Dhana yoga: the lords of wealth houses are related

text.en: Lords of the wealth-giving houses (1, 2, 5, 9, 11) are related by conjunction, mutual aspect or exchange: a dhana yoga, classically a sign of prosperity.
text.impact: A genuine money combination. Earnings, savings and gains support each other, so wealth tends to build over the years rather than staying flat.

title: The 9th lord is strong and in a kendra or trikona

text.en: The lord of the 9th house, the house of fortune, is dignified and well placed: a strong indication of fortune (akin to Lakshmi yoga).
text.impact: Good fortune supports your means: the kind of luck that shows up as timely help, a well-timed opening, or support from elders.

text.impact: The part of the chart that governs gains is well supported, so income tends to respond when you put effort in.

text.impact: Jupiter looking after your resources usually shows as timely help, generosity that comes back to you, and growth without much grasping.
